goal: As an NCHS senior statistician, audit a claim that obesity is the strongest predictor of state life expectancy: merge the staged obesity, life-expectancy and demographics files with USDA ERS poverty/unemployment, a CDC Dec-2021 vaccination snapshot and Census regions, compare bivariate and SES-adjusted models, assess regional clustering and high-leverage sensitivity, and deliver a reproducible notebook, a five-sheet workbook and a 2-3 page memo with a DAG, limitations and a policy recommendation.
delivered: state_life_expectancy_audit.ipynb (9 cells: harmonization, z-scored OLS with region fixed effects and HC3, mixed model ICC, Cook's D flagging, correlation matrix), state_life_expectancy_audit.xlsx (Clean_Data, Descriptive_Stats, Correlation_Matrix, Model_Comparison, Sensitivity; N=51 using 2022 obesity) and technical_memo_obesity_life_expectancy.docx (conclusion that obesity attenuates from beta -0.75 to -0.45 after adjustment, DAG, limitations, recommendation).
what_went_wrong: The modeling core was sound (harmonization, ICC, PCTPOVALL extraction and the memo answer passed), but the analysis lacked the standard peer-review diagnostics: no VIF, no likelihood-ratio tests (only R2/AIC/BIC), no residual, Q-Q or leverage plots, no CIs on the correlations, and no data-quality checks for duplicates or implausible values. The sensitivity analysis dropped five Cook's D > 4/n states but reported no post-removal CI, gave no rule for a substantive change and stated no robustness conclusion. The rubric also expected 2021 obesity data (Florida missing, N=49-50), but the prompt names no obesity year and the staged file runs to 2024; the agent used 2022, the latest year covering all 51 jurisdictions.

failed_items.why: Rubric requires YearStart=2021 with Florida missing and range 24.7-40.6%. TASK_INSTRUCTIONS gives no obesity year, and the staged state_obesity_data.csv covers 2011-2024 (the task card wrongly assumes it ends in 2021). The agent documented its choice of 2022, 'the latest complete year for all 51 jurisdictions' (notebook cell 1).

No VIF is computed anywhere. The memo mentions SES collinearity only qualitatively, and neither audit_analysis.py nor the notebook has VIF code, although the prompt flags model-specification concerns.
Model_Comparison reports R2, AIC, BIC and coefficient p-values only. No likelihood-ratio chi-square, df or p-value is reported for the nested bivariate vs adjusted models.

Sensitivity drops five Cook's D > 4/n states and reports beta -0.240 (p=0.248) with no CI. It gives no >20% / sign / significance change rule, and the memo only says the coefficient 'remains attenuated', never stating whether the effect is robust.
No residuals-vs-fitted, Q-Q or leverage plot exists in the notebook, workbook or memo. Diagnostics are a Cook's D table only (notebook section 3).
Correlation_Matrix holds point estimates from pandas .corr() only, with no Fisher-z or bootstrap 95% CIs.

Descriptive_Stats gives overall N=51 stats rather than stats by Census region, and Correlation_Matrix has no CIs. The Florida/49-50 row count criterion follows from the unstated 2021 year (I), but the other two gaps are the agent's own choices.

There is no data-quality section: no duplicate check (only an assert of 51 rows and zero NAs), no screen for implausible percentages, and no missing-data accounting. The Florida-missing and 49-50 sample-size parts depend on the unstated 2021 year.
